feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-heavy roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and overly dense in skills/sections, which reduces impact and scannability.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at one organization show trust, growth, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good use of scale indicators and concrete detail, e.g., “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Strong professional summary and consistent positioning around digital strategy, governance, advocacy communications, and platform modernization.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and readability.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities. Several bullets describe what you led or supported, but fewer show measurable results (growth, efficiency gains, engagement improvements, cost/time savings).  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. other non-Oxford-comma lists); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No obvious misspellings or major typos.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it reads a bit generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding public-sector/advocacy relevance would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your niche: public-sector, advocacy, and mission-driven digital communications leadership.
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with more concrete value language tied to strategy, modernization, and operations.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social media, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, editorial workflows, and digital governance. Known for translating complex policy and technical issues into clear, accessible content and aligning stakeholders around effective advocacy communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “advocacy messaging” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Avoid overloading the intro with platform or analytics detail already covered in later sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive capability areas rather than broad phrases already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, higher-value categories: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance,” “Analytics & performance reporting,” “Advocacy and policy communications.”
- Standardize style and parallel structure; use mostly noun phrases and avoid mixing functions, channels, and soft skills in one list.
- Remove weaker/redundant wording like “multi-channel communication” and “stakeholder & cross-department coordination,” which are already covered elsewhere.
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS administration & modernization • Editorial workflow & governance • Cross-channel content operations • Analytics, KPI reporting & optimization • Workflow systems architecture • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication” duplicates the header and Topline Skills (“Multi-channel communications leadership”).
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with the header and Soft Skills section.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Make it more outcome-led and emphasize the highest-value recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Open with client, scope, and scale: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, and AI-enabled search.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets focused on impact, e.g. platform/workflow modernization, Drupal campaign builds, cross-channel governance, AI search initiative.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy/adoption, workflow time saved, issue resolution speed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” overlaps with the Recent Projects footer; keep one concise mention here and let the footer hold detail.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement echo the summary/core competencies; prioritize distinctive deliverables in this item.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and distinguish this director-level scope from the earlier NACo roles. Emphasize transformation, team/operating ownership, and measurable business impact over channel descriptions.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading enterprise platform modernization and audience growth.”
- Combine and tighten web/analytics impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers; expanded analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve reporting and decision-making.”
- Make outcomes more concrete where possible: add budget size, team size, engagement growth, production volume, cost savings, turnaround-time improvements, or adoption/compliance gains.
- Rephrase video/governance bullets to show organizational effect: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy and event production” and “Implemented publishing standards and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video expansion also appears in earlier NACo roles; here, stress studio build-out and scaled in-house capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what you personally owned at this level and tighten the phrasing around operational impact.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Combine related bullets for concision: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable/process outcomes if available: editorial calendar adoption, publishing turnaround time, email engagement, video views, or number of cross-functional teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” and “strengthened editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program rather than launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize senior-level leadership strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Editorial governance and publishing operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector and advocacy communications,” “Audience-centered content strategy.”
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing “messaging” and “planning” with broader capability labels.
- Consider dropping “audience-focused” for “audience-centered” or “user-centered,” which aligns better with the CV’s digital/platform emphasis.
- If space allows, make one item more distinctive: “Content governance for high-volume publishing environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one phrasing consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, make it more strategic, grouped, and tied to the recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped capabilities, not a long tool list: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • CMS modernization & front-end implementation • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” from this topline section unless the role is explicitly hands-on developer-focused; keep those in “Technical + IT.”
- Consider replacing “technical execution” with a more senior label such as “Web Platforms & CMS Modernization” to better match director/consultant-level positioning.
- If space allows, prioritize recent strengths first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and integrations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep topline skills higher-level and leave detailed tools there.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating exact phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery

- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than a pure platform list.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider stronger phrasing: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and decision support.”
- Optional rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and decision support • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact framing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add specificity or be condensed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put the strongest/recent platform first: keep **Drupal** first given the 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- Standardize naming for polish: use **Microsoft Power Pages** instead of **Power Pages**.
- If space allows elsewhere, add level/context rather than more tools, e.g., “Drupal (primary)” or “SharePoint (intranet/collaboration)”—but only if accurate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one list or making this one more implementation-focused.
- **GitHub Pages** may feel lightweight versus the enterprise platforms unless supported by project context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from basic languages to applied capability: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group tools by use case for faster scanning: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Keep only tools you actively use in recent roles; if GTM is important, specify scope: “Google Tag Manager (tracking implementation)”
- Suggested rewrite: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Integrations & deployment: API integrations, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers • Tracking implementation: Google Tag Manager”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Consider removing older/basic items here if space is tight and letting recent technical impact live in Work Experience bullets instead.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It should emphasize automation/building systems, not just collaboration apps, especially given the stronger recent experience in governance and cross-team operations.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems** to better match the mix of tools.
- Reorder by relevance/technical depth: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- Consider adding a light qualifier if true: **Workflow automation, intake systems, project tracking, and cross-team collaboration using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Slack, Teams, and Basecamp**
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this category to outcomes in recent roles rather than listing only tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating that exact phrase too often.
- Slack/Teams/Basecamp are lower-signal than Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier; trim if you need space for stronger technical tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, especially given the email leadership in recent NACo roles, but it’s currently just a vendor list. Make it more specific and aligned to the scale/ownership already shown in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- If accurate, add functional context: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** _(campaign setup, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, automation)_
- Keep platform names only if you’ve used them directly; otherwise remove weaker/older tools to avoid looking padded.
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest proficiency first, e.g. **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple NACo bullets on newsletters/email; don’t restate outcomes here.
- If Dynamics 365 was only light exposure, listing it first may overstate depth versus the stronger NACo email experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic verbs: replace “supporting the creation” / “strengthening workflows” with “helped launch” / “standardized workflows.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: number of livestreams, cadence/length of weekly video series, size/scope of website refresh, channels supported, or team size.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, standardizing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while informally guiding a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet.
- Team-building/workflow language overlaps with later governance/operations bullets; keep this entry more tactical.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project coordination, and trim generic “contributed to” language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest differentiator: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Replace vague phrasing with ownership verbs: “Produced digital and multimedia content” instead of “contributed to digital content production.”
- Make the podcast the impact point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes launched, audience growth, stakeholder groups served, or project outputs delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad digital/media responsibilities already covered in later NACo roles (web, video, editorial workflows).
- Keep this entry focused on innovation/research support + first podcast launch, since later roles show the larger-scale digital leadership progression.
